title: Cline operating card
summary: This intermediate reference explains why the operating guidance cannot yet be safely corrected and identifies the evidence needed to complete the source update without inventing instructions.
prerequisites: Access to the current resource file and its repository history
Access to current official Cline documentation

sections.title: Can I safely use this operating card?
paragraphs: No. The supplied material does not contain the existing operating instructions or a successfully verified replacement for the changed citation, so no Cline procedure can be confirmed. This is an intermediate-level source review, not verified operational guidance.

The citation record supplied for review is content/resources/coding-tools/cline-operating-card.json. That is a local resource path rather than an HTTPS product source. Whether an earlier source moved or merely passed its review cadence is UNKNOWN. Its replacement URL and the claims it previously supported are also UNKNOWN, so affected operational claims are omitted rather than guessed.
The existing resource text was not supplied. Consequently, which material is unaffected by the source change is UNKNOWN, and no claim can be represented as preserved verbatim.
sections.callout: Do not infer commands, interface labels, versions, configuration keys, or recovery actions from this card. Verify each operational claim against accessible official documentation before use.

sections.title: Complete the source correction
paragraphs: Step 1: Retrieve the current cline-operating-card.json file and its revision history. If either is unavailable, stop and request repository access or a verbatim copy from the resource owner. Do not reconstruct the missing text.

Step 2: Identify the former HTTPS citation, its replacement, and every sentence it supported. If the former citation or its replacement cannot be identified, consult the source-review record or repository history and leave the affected claims marked UNKNOWN until an authoritative source is available.

Step 3: Open the official Cline source that directly supports each affected claim and compare the documented behavior with the existing wording. If a URL does not resolve or the documentation does not support a claim, omit that claim and record the unresolved evidence gap instead of substituting an undocumented procedure.

Step 4: Change only the citation metadata and wording invalidated by the source change. If unaffected text cannot be distinguished from affected text, stop and request the prior review record rather than rewriting the guide.

Step 5: Validate the completed file as JSON and against the Resource schema, then review the diff. If parsing or schema validation fails, correct the reported field or JSON syntax and rerun validation. If the diff contains unrelated edits, revert them before publication.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: The expected evidence is a minimal diff that names the former citation, records its resolving HTTPS replacement, identifies the claims affected by the change, and leaves every unaffected byte unchanged.

Verify the result by opening every listed source over HTTPS, checking each affected statement against the cited first-party page, parsing the committed file as JSON, running the catalogue schema validation, and confirming that the final diff contains no formatting or editorial changes unrelated to the citation correction.

That evidence is not present in the supplied material. Completion status is therefore UNKNOWN until the current file, source history, replacement citation, affected claims, and successful validation results are available.
